name: Francisco Franco
role: Spanish general and dictator, Caudillo of Spain (1936–1975)
summary: Franco led the 1936 military rising and ruled Spain as head of state and government until his death. He built a Catholic, anti-communist, nationalist regime with a single movement, vertical syndicates, organic representation and a monarchy of his design, suppressing parties, unions and regional autonomy. He kept Spain neutral in World War II, then aligned with the United States and opened the economy from 1959.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mixed: the 1938 labour charter subordinated the economy to national politics and denounced liberal capitalism, while it also recognised private initiative as a source of economic life; from 1959 his speeches embraced exports, foreign investment and the Common Market.

public-ownership.rationale: The 1938 Fuero del Trabajo he issued says the State will not itself be an entrepreneur except where private initiative is lacking or the supreme national interest requires it.

unions-good.rationale: He valued the state-run vertical syndicates as organs of national production and social justice, but outlawed independent unions; evidence points both ways on unions as such.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Fuero del Trabajo and the 1958 Principles recognise private property but make it conditional on its social function and subordinate to the nation's interest.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He said he rejected capitalism because he hated the abuse of the powerful, and the labour charter put the firm under State supervision and subordinated capital to the common good.

cut-welfare.rationale: His labour charter and 1945 Fuero promised expanded social insurance (old age, illness, unemployment, maternity) and a family subsidy; there is no sign he saw welfare as creating dependency.

worker-ownership.rationale: The labour charter gives the head of the firm sole direction and responsibility to the State and contrasts craft production with 'Marxist herding'; he denounced collectivism.

strong-leader.rationale: He ruled as Caudillo with all powers, demanded loyalty to the Head of State, and blamed party gridlock and ministerial turnover for the pre-1936 collapse.

state-harmful.rationale: The 1937 decree speaks of building the 'new totalitarian State' and the labour charter calls the State a totalitarian instrument at the service of the homeland.

empower-police-military.rationale: The 1958 Principles state the Armies must have the strength needed for their service, and his speeches describe the armed institutions and police as faithful guardians of the regime.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Evidence is indirect: reference accounts say the regime's vagrancy law was used to criminalise prostitution in 1954 as part of enforcing Catholic morality.

decide-locally.rationale: He treated the municipality as a natural entity of representation, but insisted on the intangible unity of Spain and eliminated regional autonomy in practice.

traditional-family.rationale: The 1945 Fuero recognises the family as the natural foundation of society with rights above all positive law, declares marriage one and indissoluble and protects large families.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred: from his insistence on one and indissoluble Catholic marriage and the regime's criminalisation of homosexuality (1954); he never addressed same-sex marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred: from his declaration that legislation must follow the Law of God according to the Catholic Church (1958 Principles); he did not address abortion directly.

more-religion-public.rationale: The 1945 Fuero makes Catholicism the State religion with official protection; the 1958 Principles bind legislation to Catholic doctrine; his speeches call Spain a Catholic State.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He proclaimed Spain's historical tradition and Catholic faith as the inalienable inheritance to be handed on, and fused 'tradition' into the new State.

gradual-change.rationale: Mixed: he rejected 'utopias and risky projects' and invoked tradition, yet repeatedly called his movement a revolution and said it 'instaurated' rather than restored.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He denounced the 1946 UN condemnation of Spain as a farce driven by Masonic and communist intrigue; he later sought UN entry (1955-56) as a sovereign member.

free-trade.rationale: He said no people can live from its own economy alone and by 1959 urged Spain to compete abroad and join the European market, but the earlier autarkic policy and the labour charter's protection of national work point the other way.

nation-first.rationale: He insisted on Spanish sovereignty and independence against UN pressure, yet also said Spain should serve the common interest of Europe and the West.

limit-growth.rationale: His speeches celebrate economic growth, industrialisation and development plans as the regime's main achievements; the 1958 Principles call for intensified industrialisation.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: He said liberal-capitalist progress brought technical gains without moral progress or fair distribution, and that technology cannot be separated from spirit.

revolution-justified.rationale: Contested: he led an armed uprising that he called a crusade and 'national revolution', while condemning the revolutions of 1934 and 1936 as communist subversion.

experts-over-public.rationale: Appointing technocrats is an action, not a stated view on experts versus the public.

central-planning.rationale: He denounced the Soviet 'State-employer' as bureaucratic and dehumanising and the labour charter keeps private initiative primary, though he ran development plans.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The labour charter promises protection of national work and early policy was autarkic, but from 1959 he urged competition abroad and Common Market membership.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He described State credit policy that steers credit toward sectors that need it, and the labour charter orders credit to develop national wealth and small property.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The labour charter commits the State to multiply family home, land holding and tools of work, to give each peasant family a plot and to let land pass to those who farm it; it contrasts this with capitalist concentration.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: His labour charter sets wages and rejects Marxism; he repeatedly opposed any abolition of the wage system.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The 1938 labour charter organises all economic factors into State-led vertical syndicates, and the 1958 Principles list the syndicate as a basic natural entity.

one-party-rule.rationale: His 1937 decree merged Falange and Carlists into one national political entity under his leadership and dissolved all other parties, though he insisted it was a movement, not a party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The 1947 Law of Succession declares Spain a kingdom; in 1958 and 1964 he called the 'traditional, Catholic, social and representative' monarchy the best fit for his doctrine.

democracy-best.rationale: He called liberal party democracy 'inorganic' and a cause of Spain's decline, and offered 'organic democracy' through family, municipality and syndicate instead.

direct-votes.rationale: He submitted the Law of Succession to a referendum and required referendum approval to change fundamental laws, but otherwise ruled through decrees and appointed Cortes.

workers-councils.rationale: He rejected Soviet-style rule and Marxist class organisation, offering instead vertical syndicates under the State.

right-to-secede.rationale: The 1958 Principles declare the unity of Spain's men and lands intangible; his 1975 testament asks Spaniards to keep the unity of the lands of Spain.

natural-rulers.rationale: An emphasis on hierarchy is nearby; he did not state that some are naturally suited to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: He led an armed rising he called a crusade and justified it as national salvation; he did not hold that political violence is never justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: He said soldiers love peace because they know war's horrors, but also praised adversity and the Crusade as forging the nation's virility.

separate-church-state.rationale: The 1945 Fuero makes Catholicism the State religion; he described Spain as a Catholic State in friendly collaboration with the Church.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The 1958 Principles say the nation honours the Law of God according to Catholic Church doctrine, which will inspire its legislation (Church doctrine rather than scripture itself).

private-courts-defense.rationale: The labour charter states that justice in labour matters belongs to the State, and his speeches praise the State's armed and judicial institutions.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He repeatedly denounced class struggle as the poison of Spanish politics and called for class cooperation.

civilizational-union.rationale: He promoted the Hispanic family of peoples and an Iberian pact, though not as a political union.

self-interest-moral.rationale: His charters present work as service and duty to the homeland and subordinate individual interests to the common good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The 1945 Fuero lists Spaniards' duties first (loyalty to the Head of State, obedience, military service) and the 1958 Principles subordinate individual interests to the nation's good.

limit-population.rationale: The Fuero protects large families and the regime paid family subsidies.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: His programme prides itself on industrialisation, hydraulic works and technological modernisation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred: from his insistence that modernisation proceed within tradition and the established institutions and that the revolution not destroy.

restore-past-order.rationale: He said the movement was not a return to the archaic: 'instaurar y no restaurar', taking the living substance of tradition and modernising it.

results-over-ideology.rationale: His 1937 decree called the movement 'not rigid or static', open to revision as reality advises; yet he also insisted on fixed, 'immutable' principles.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred: from the 1958 Principles' goal of intensifying industrialisation and scientific research.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Inferred: from the labour charter's hierarchy of professions organised into branch syndicates.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The labour charter ties pay to work and responsibility, with a family wage and subsidy; there is no distribution according to need as a principle.

profit-exploitation.rationale: He said the capitalist way lives from exploiting the worker, but the labour charter accepts business profit and a just interest on capital.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He denounced the Soviet system as a bureaucratic tyranny and communism as a substantive evil.

collective-farming.rationale: The labour charter promotes family plots, tenant stability and land ownership by those who farm it, and rejects Marxist 'herding'.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Fuero says Spaniards contribute to public burdens according to ability and taxes need a law voted in the Cortes.

harm-principle.rationale: The Fuero allows free expression only while it does not attack the fundamental principles of the State and bars exercising rights against the nation's unity.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Fuero treats the person as a member of the national community with duties and gives families and natural entities rights above positive law.

conscription.rationale: The 1945 Fuero makes military service a title of honour and obligatory when called by law.

positive-liberty.rationale: He said liberty is impaired by real states of poverty and that political freedom without economic means is a mockery.

media-academia-power.rationale: His Masonry articles claim Masons own the major newspapers, hold university chairs and judicial posts and so dominate politics; this is his own claim, not a general theory.

organic-representation.rationale: The 1958 Principles and the Fuero provide for representation through family, municipality and syndicate, and declare other political organisations illegal.

total-state.rationale: His 1937 decree and the labour charter called the State totalitarian and subordinated the economy to politics, but later texts keep private initiative, the Church's independence and 'authority, liberty and service'.

national-rebirth.rationale: He framed the rising as a 'National Revolution' to end Spain's political decadence and rebuild its unity and greatness.

territorial-expansion.rationale: At Hendaye (1940) he reportedly demanded French Morocco and Gibraltar for entering the war, but later speeches stress peace and a defensive posture.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The Fuero requires loyalty to the Head of State and the Law of Succession requires oaths to the fundamental laws; this is a modern oath, not a feudal bond.

bound-labor.rationale: The labour charter wants tenants secure and land to pass to those who work it, with no bound labour owed to a lord.

universal-morality.rationale: The 1958 Principles speak of man as bearer of eternal values and of obeying God's Law as the one true faith.

single-common-good.rationale: He argued that individual and group interests must always be subordinate to the common good of the nation and that parties divide it.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The labour charter makes the firm head solely responsible for management; workers get only information on production.

national-self-determination.rationale: He backed Moroccan independence in 1956 while denying Basque or Catalan self-rule.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The 1958 Principles base the nation's legislation on Catholic faith, and his Masonry articles blame rationalist secular currents for Spain's decline.

class-collaboration.rationale: He said the movement seeks cooperation of social classes rather than their divorce, and the Principles call the firm a community of interests.

workers-nation.rationale: The labour charter and the Falange programme he adopted called the State 'National' and 'Syndicalist', bringing workers into the national State.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The labour charter promises to free the married woman from workshop and factory; the Law of Succession reserves the Crown to males.

ban-interest.rationale: The labour charter persecutes usury but speaks of a just return on capital and credit to small business, not banning interest.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He rejected the Marxist view of the State, presenting it as an arbiter above classes, as the 'link between State and Society'.

proportional-representation.rationale: He rejected representation through parties; the 1958 Principles declare any political organisation outside the organic system illegal.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He denounced the pre-1936 governing classes as decadent and called party politicians 'politicastros'.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The labour charter gives the State a leading role in the economy and social policy.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Fuero says the law protects all Spaniards equally and respects human dignity, but it limited non-Catholic worship and excluded those who opposed the regime.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: He said the State acts on Catholic doctrine in mixed matters such as marriage and teaching.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He criticised majority rule as 'inorganic' and relied on plebiscites only for his own constitutional laws.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: He led the 1936 uprising and justified it as a crusade.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: He said he wants cooperation, not 'constant rivalry' and competition among social actors.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: His 1937 decree dissolved all other parties and the 1939 and 1940 laws outlawed Popular Front parties, Masonry and communism.

separated-powers.rationale: He held all powers of the new State from 1936 and called some of the powers in his person intransferable, though he praised judicial independence.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The labour charter treats acts that disturb production as crimes of 'lesa patria' and bans disruptions of production.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The Fuero says public offices go by merit and capacity.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Article 35 of the Fuero lets the Government suspend key liberties by decree-law.

party-controls-media.rationale: The regime ran a Movement press and radio and the Fuero limits expression to the State's fundamental principles.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: He said Movement members freely pledge themselves to a discipline and a leadership.

head-commands-forces.rationale: His 1937 decree names the Head of State supreme chief of the Militia and from 1936 he held command and chose ministers.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Inferred: from his respect for the hierarchy and the concordat of 1953 recognising Church rights.

clerical-rule.rationale: He said Church and State are two independent perfect societies, each sovereign in its order.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Inferred: from his demand for loyalty to the Fatherland and obedience to laws.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Reference accounts say the regime enforced Catholic values; the 1958 Principles speak of improving moral health.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: His own lifelong rule is not a stated view on presidential re-election.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He signed the 1953 agreements with the US granting bases and the Iberian Pact with Portugal and praised them.

people-in-arms.rationale: The 1937 decree merged militias into an auxiliary Militia of the Army, and the Principles call for strong professional armies.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred: from his presentation of Christian Hispanic civilization as the true cause of Europe.

death-penalty.rationale: Reference accounts record that his regime executed many opponents, including militants in 1975.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred: from the 1958 Principles on the moral health of Spaniards and Catholic enforcement of public morality.

minority-language-support.rationale: His government revoked the official recognition the Republic had given to Basque, Galician and Catalan and ran schooling and media in Spanish only.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: In 1950s speeches he urged long-term solidarity and aid to economically weak areas, replacing exploitation.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Under the Law of Succession the head of state is the Caudillo and then a king or regent chosen by the Council and Cortes.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Fuero del Trabajo XII and the 1958 Principles subject all property to the nation's interest and its social function.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He said the Church has its own sovereignty; he guaranteed it through the 1953 concordat.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: He claimed the Movement was not a party and the head of state stood above factions, though he led the single party.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: He called separatism part of Spain's disintegration and treated unity as intangible.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Regional autonomy was abolished and the Basque fueros ended in two provinces, though kept in Navarre and Alava.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Contested: the regime styled him 'Caudillo by the grace of God' with ceremonial honours, but not divine descent.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Law of Succession requires the monarch to swear the fundamental laws and the Fuero demands legal security, though in practice he ruled by decree.

leader-cult.rationale: His portrait was on coins and stamps, he was greeted with mass chants and the title 'Caudillo'.

land-redistribution.rationale: The labour charter aims for land to pass to those who farm it 'in just conditions', and the Fuero requires compensation for expropriation.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: He eliminated regional autonomy and recognition of minority languages.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: He rejected materialism and said more matter does not ennoble, only spirit does.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: His early policy was autarkic, yet he stated that no people can live from its economy alone and abandoned autarky in 1959.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He spoke of Spain's civilising mission in Morocco and America but also repudiated old colonialist moulds.

patriotic-education.rationale: He addressed youth organisations on service to the Fatherland; the Principles make service to its unity a sacred duty.

former-empire-influence.rationale: He promoted Hispanidad, seeing Spain as the cultural bridge and head of the Hispanic family of peoples.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Fuero lists rights and fundamental laws need a referendum to change, but the government could suspend key articles.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Law of Succession makes the head of state hereditary or appointed.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: from his rejection of party pluralism and demand that all obey national unity.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred: from the Fuero's duty of loyalty to the Head of State and obedience to the laws.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Cortes were subordinate to the Head of State, who held decree power.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The 1958 Principles call service to the Fatherland a sacred duty and collective task of all Spaniards.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: He said Spain started development without foreign aid but then accepted US aid.

return-lost-territory.rationale: He demanded the return of Gibraltar to Spain.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: His regime was founded on the 1936 uprising and the Falange programme and he rejected anti-fascism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: He condemned communism but rejected comparisons that put his regime alongside the defeated Axis.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: He said Spain should find its own 'style and solutions' and called party democracy unsuited to it.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Principles call the armies the guarantee of security, and the Law of Succession places the army chief on the Regency Council.

office-by-exam.rationale: The Fuero and the Principles open offices by merit and capacity.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: His later speeches welcome foreign capital and investment.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The 1945 Fuero declares marriage one and indissoluble.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Fuero protects private property including land holdings.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Fuero says no tax may be imposed except by a law voted in the Cortes.

single-official-language.rationale: The regime made Spanish the exclusive language of schooling and the media and withdrew recognition from other languages.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The Fuero commits the State to protect large families and the labour charter promises a family subsidy.

job-guarantee.rationale: The labour charter and the Fuero say every Spaniard has a right to work and the State must satisfy it.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Fuero lists obedience to the laws as a duty of Spaniards.

industrial-unions.rationale: The labour charter organises syndicates by branch of production.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Reference accounts say he firmly believed in a Jewish-Masonic-Bolshevik conspiracy against Spain; his own writings and 1940 law pin national decline on Masonry.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Fuero declares marriage indissoluble and protects the family.

religious-nation.rationale: The 1958 Principles call the Catholic faith 'inseparable from the national conscience'.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: He spoke of solidarity between regions and directed development to poorer regions.

defeat-communism.rationale: He called communism a substantive evil that must be resisted and outlawed it in 1940.

religion-illusion.rationale: His speeches present faith as the basis of the nation and Marxism as materialist error.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: He said the liberal-capitalist order raised wealth and technology but without moral progress or fair distribution.

socialized-care.rationale: The labour charter and Fuero place care in the family and free the married woman from factory work.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He said 'we want neither Marxism nor capitalism' and the labour charter calls itself a reaction against both.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Reference accounts say the regime's vagrancy law was used to make homosexuality a criminal offence in 1954.

suppress-opposition.rationale: His 1937 decree dissolved all other parties and the 1939 and 1940 laws penalised opponents; unions and opposition were suppressed.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The 1945 Fuero barred public ceremonies of other religions; the 1967 revision committed the State to protect religious freedom within morality and public order.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: He said Spanish America was not a colony and repudiated old colonialist moulds in 1956.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: He called the division into right and left artificial and the cause of ruin and presented the Movement as above it.

islam-incompatible.rationale: He stressed affinity with the Arab world through blood and spirit.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He ruled as Caudillo 'by the grace of God' and promulgated laws conscious of responsibility before God.

social-market-economy.rationale: He proposed a third way keeping private initiative with social justice.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He was neutral in World War II, but after 1953 aligned with the US and called Spain a key point of Western resistance.

dynastic-succession.rationale: He established a monarchy and designated Juan Carlos as his successor.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Fuero requires acts under preestablished norms and sentences under prior law, though he governed by decree.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He criticised the 'disproportionate supremacy of a false minority' and abuse of the powerful.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The regime's criminal law is not his stated view on military service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: He called atheism a Masonic and Marxist error and made Catholicism the State religion.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: He praised the order forces and armed institutions as guardians of the regime and ran a system of political imprisonment.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The Fuero backs Church and private charities but also promises state social insurance.

term-limits.rationale: His own lifelong rule is not a stated view on term limits.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: from the Fuero reserving participation to Spaniards.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The regime ran the Frente de Juventudes, which he addressed.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: He agreed to US bases in 1953 and praised the agreements.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Principles call work the origin of hierarchy and honour, though capital gets a just return.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Principles define the nation as made of past, present and future generations and the 1937 decree invokes the secular regime that forged its unity.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The 1937 decree invokes the 'heroes and martyrs' who fell.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: He framed the war as a crusade and quoted that where God leaves a State the demon enters.

independent-unions.rationale: The labour charter puts unions under State direction and independent unions were banned.

family-wage.rationale: The labour charter and Fuero require pay sufficient for the worker and family.

person-over-state.rationale: The Fuero opens with respect for human dignity but subordinates rights to the nation's unity and common good.

spiritual-nature.rationale: He called man a bearer of eternal values and said politics must serve spirit.

racial-pride.rationale: He spoke of the Hispanic 'racial community' with pride.

language-defines-nation.rationale: He described the Hispanic peoples as united by one language, faith and blood.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: He spoke of an international conspiracy against Spain.

collective-bargaining.rationale: He cited collective syndical agreements as part of social policy.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: He urged that Afro-Asian peoples share fairly in their resources and an end to colonialist moulds.

sacred-nation.rationale: The 1937 decree speaks of the sacred name of the fallen and the Principles of the sacred duty to the unity of the Fatherland.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The Fuero and Principles ground the person in eternal values.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The Principles call the Catholic faith the only true one.

farm-price-support.rationale: The labour charter commits to regulating farm prices to ensure a minimum profit.

workers-own-party.rationale: He dissolved all parties in 1937 and offered one national organisation.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The labour charter places all economic factors in compulsory vertical syndicates.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Fuero gave Catholicism official status and barred other public worship.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: He defined democracy as effective service and organic participation instead of competitive elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred: from his Catholic moral stance and the Fuero's marriage doctrine.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Fuero says all Spaniards may hold office, but the Crown was reserved to males.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: from his view of the Catholic faith and family as the foundation of society; he never addressed this claim.

indirect-election.rationale: Council of the Realm members were elected by groups within the Cortes rather than by direct vote.

national-church-status.rationale: The Fuero declares the Catholic religion the State's and protects it officially.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: He abolished the autonomy granted by the Republic and treated separatism as a root of decline.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The Principles call the unity of the men and lands of Spain intangible and the nation a community of past generations.

close-ties-china.rationale: Anti-communism is a label, not a stated view on ties with China.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: He abolished parties and built a single movement.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: He said tradition must be modernised and technology joined with spirit.

national-resource-control.rationale: The 1958 Principles call for safeguarding mining resources.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The Fuero puts family rights above positive law.

notes: Laws of the regime (labour charter 1938, Fuero 1945, Law of Succession 1947, Principles 1958, 1939-40 repression laws) are cited as his record because he issued or promulgated them and held decree power; the Fuero del Trabajo was drafted by the Falange council. Speeches are from an official anthology (to 1964) and 1937 collection; later years rely on the 1975 testament and reference accounts. Positions shifted on autarky (abandoned 1959), religious freedom (1967 revision) and Marxist 'totalitarian State' language (1937-38 versus later).
